title: Build your own text adventure

series.title: Voice-Powered Video Games (5 classes)
series.summary: Classic games, rebuilt with your voice. Every session starts with a game you play out loud, then gives you the tools to build your own with Deepgram. Part 1: Zork I (1980) and a text adventure of your own. Part 2: Unscanned, a stealth game where every character is a live voice agent.

summary: Invent and build your own Zork-style text adventure. A voice story coach interviews you about your plot and turns it into a game that works; the code sits beside you to read and change; and you play it, and Zork itself, by voice.
detail: Zork I (1980) is the text adventure that started it all, and Microsoft released it under the MIT licence in 2025, so you start by playing it, right at the top of this page, by voice. Then you make your own. A story coach (a Deepgram Voice Agent: Flux listens, Claude asks, a Flux voice speaks) interviews you about your setting, hero, villain, places, puzzles and ending, and builds a small game that it checks can actually be won. Your whole game is one readable file in a code panel beside you. You never have to touch it, but if you want to code, change any line and press Run. Then play it out loud.
outcome: Your own text adventure: a plot you invented, turned into a playable game you can win, read, edit and play by voice, and a game.js file to take home.
artifact: game.js: your adventure as one readable file, plus a game that runs in your browser on your own Deepgram key.
prereqs: A laptop with Google Chrome and a microphone.
Headphones or earbuds. The coach and the game both talk, and headphones stop the mic hearing them.
A free Deepgram account and API key. Use the sign-up QR code at your table.
A story idea is welcome but not needed: the coach will help you find one.

flow.title: Play first: Zork I
flow.note: Before you build anything, play the original. Paste your Deepgram key, press Start Zork, then Talk, and say what you want to do: "open the mailbox", "read the leaflet", "go north". Stuck? Press Hint. Ten minutes is plenty: notice the places, the things you pick up, and the problems you solve with them.

flow.title: Your game studio
flow.note: Now make your own. Your key carries over. Talk your story through with the coach until it builds your game, then play it. The code panel on the right is your game: read it, change it, press Run. (The Play Zork tab is still there if you want another look.)

sections.title: 1 · Get inspired
sections.summary: Ten minutes in the Great Underground Empire.

steps.title: Play Zork by voice
steps.instruction: Open the Play Zork tab, press Start Zork, then Talk. Try "open the mailbox", "read the leaflet", "go north". Notice what makes it fun: places, things to pick up, and problems you solve with them.
steps.check: You have heard the narrator read at least three rooms.

sections.title: 2 · Plan your story
sections.summary: The coach asks one question at a time and shapes your answers into a plot that works.

steps.title: Talk to the coach
steps.instruction: Open Plan your story and press Talk to the coach (or type). Answer its questions: where it happens, who you are, what you want, what stands in the way, the places, the puzzles and the ending.
steps.check: The coach has read your plot back to you.

steps.title: Let it build
steps.instruction: Say "build it". The coach adds your rooms, items and puzzles one by one, then checks the game can be won. If something blocks the ending, it tells you and fixes it.
steps.check: A yellow note says your game is in the code panel and can be won.

sections.title: 3 · Build and play
sections.summary: Play it, find what feels wrong, change it.

steps.title: Play your game
steps.instruction: Press ▶ Run, then Talk. Play to the end.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.instruction: Change something in the code: a room description, a new item, a new exit. Press ▶ Run. The line under the code tells you if anything is broken, by line number. Or ask the coach: "add a secret passage behind the bookcase".
steps.check: Your change shows up when you play.

steps.title: Take it home
steps.instruction: Press Download to save game.js. It is plain data, so you can keep building it anywhere.
steps.check: game.js is in your Downloads folder.

troubleshooting: Nothing happens when I talk: check Chrome is allowed to use the microphone (the icon at the left of the address bar). You can always type instead.
The coach or the game keeps interrupting itself: the mic is hearing the speaker. Put headphones on.
The coach says it could not connect: your Deepgram key needs Voice Agent access and some credit. Check the key was pasted whole.
The coach is slow to build: it adds each room, item and puzzle separately, so a game takes a minute or so. Watch the Building… line count up.
Red lines under the code: that is the game telling you what is broken and on which line, usually a missing comma or quote, or a name that does not match.
My game was replaced: Example replaces your game with the starter. Download yours first; your latest code is also kept in this browser.
